questions.question: So, who are you?
questions.answer: A frontend engineer in Berlin who started out in UX. I like interfaces that stay calm when things go wrong.

scene.caption: Two views of the same person

questions.question: Where did you start?
questions.answer: Studying it taught me to ask what someone needs to understand — and what they’ll do next.

questions.question: How did you end up in frontend?
questions.lead: I learned to build what I drew.
questions.answer: The states, the interactions, the implementation. I stopped handing designs over and started finishing them.

questions.question: What do you do at F24?
questions.answer: Crisis-management software, used when things are already going wrong. I built the original Svelte frontend and I’ve kept delivering in React since.

questions.question: What did four years there teach you?
questions.answer: Keep the rows on screen when a request fails. Ignore answers that arrive out of date. Put keyboard focus back where it was. Small promises, big difference.

questions.question: What do you build for yourself?
questions.answer: Second Voice rewrites your writing and shows exactly what changed. Flow turns spoken requests into calendar actions you can still edit.

scene.caption: My own products, end to end

questions.question: What do you love doing?
questions.lead: Making complicated things simple to see.
questions.answer: DNS, TLS, containers, a single web request — drawn so they finally click, and useful enough to come back to.

questions.question: What do you care about in code?
questions.answer: Typed contracts, real tests, accessibility, performance. No portfolio theatre.

ending.label: And finally
ending.question: Can we talk?
ending.answer: If you’re building something people rely on when things go wrong, I’d love to hear about it.
